subject: A new paper using Stan in Epidemics

messages.author: c80c69de54446223
messages.subject: A new paper using Stan in Epidemics
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm not sure if it's the right place (though it should be). As a quiet but long-time follower of Stan and Stan-related people (such as Andrew's awesome blog and your recent PK/PD conference in Paris), I wanted to share with you my first paper using Stan. I heard that you were collecting them at some point. I'm not aware of other Stan-users in my particular field (epidemiology of transmissible diseases), but I'm doing as much advertising as I can!

Thanks again for such an amazing tool!
Best regards,

Julien Riou
Université Pierre et Marie Curie, Paris, France

messages.author: c80c69de54446223
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] A new paper using Stan in Epidemiology
parts:
Good!

Maybe I should develop a little, as it may be useful for others here: it's basically a SIR model transformed into a negative-binomial regression model with a hierarchical structure, and we used it to jointly model several epidemics of Zika and Chikungunya (two diseases with very similar transmission routes) that successively occurred in the same areas in 2013-2015. We also used LOOIC for model comparison. The Stan code is available in the appendix if anyone is interested!

Cheers,
Julien
